app.tagline: Find junk that's safe to remove. Nothing is deleted until you choose to.
clean.title: Clean up
clean.progress: Moving to the Recycle Bin… {0} of {1}
clean.intro: Click Scan to see what can be cleaned. Scanning only looks — nothing is changed.
clean.folder.title: Clean up a folder
clean.folder.nothing: Nothing to clean in this folder.
clean.folder.truncated: This folder is very large: only the first {0} folders were looked through.
clean.folder.Missing: This folder can't be found. It may have been moved or deleted.
clean.folder.SystemFolder: This folder holds Windows, installed programs or app data, so it isn't scanned. Choose a project or document folder instead.
clean.folder.NotLocalFixedDrive: Only folders on this PC's own disks can be cleaned, not USB drives or network folders.
space.title: Disk space
space.subtitle: See what takes up the space on a drive or in a folder. Scanning only reads; anything you tick goes through the same list, Recycle Bin and undo as a clean.
space.intro: Pick a drive or a folder, then press Scan. A whole system drive takes a minute or two.
space.unreadable: {0} folders could not be read (other users' folders, protected system folders); what is inside them is not counted.
space.unaccounted: Windows reports {1} used on {0}; {2} was found here. The other {3} is mostly in places that can't be read, such as System Restore points.
space.kinds.note: Grouped by file extension, as scanned. Moving things does not update these totals; scan again for that.
space.note: Ticked items are listed first; nothing moves until you confirm. Windows, programs and app data can't be moved from here.
space.moved: {0} items ({1}) moved to the Recycle Bin.
space.movedSkipped: {0} items ({1}) moved to the Recycle Bin; {2} were not moved.
space.why.SystemOrAppData: Windows, programs or app data can't be moved from here
space.why.PersonalFolder: This personal folder stays; what is inside it can be moved
space.why.HiddenSystem: Hidden system file, can't be moved
clean.appRunning: {0} is open — close it to clean this
clean.moreItems: {0} smaller items ({1}) are not listed one by one; they are cleaned together with this category.
clean.note: Selected items go to the Recycle Bin, and you can undo a clean with one click.
clean.done: Moved {0} items ({1}) to the Recycle Bin.
clean.doneSkipped: Moved {0} items ({1}) to the Recycle Bin. {2} were left alone because they changed, are in use, or their app is open.
review.title: Review what will be moved
review.note: Everything below goes to the Recycle Bin. Untick anything you want to keep. Nothing is moved until you confirm, and you can undo it afterwards.
undo.done: Put back {0} items from the Recycle Bin.
undo.partial: Put back {0} items. {1} could not be put back: no longer in the Recycle Bin, or something with the same name is already in its place.
history.desc: The last 5 cleans. Undo puts what was moved back where it was, as long as it is still in the Recycle Bin.
exclude.desc: Scans leave these out, and nothing inside them is ever moved. Add a folder here, or press the lock next to an item on the Clean up page.
exclude.hidden: Left out: {0} on the Never clean list
cat.temp-files.name: Temporary files
cat.temp-files.desc: Files programs leave in your temp folder. Only items untouched for a day are listed; programs create new ones when they need them.
cat.crash-dumps.name: Crash dumps
cat.crash-dumps.desc: Memory snapshots saved when an app crashed. Only useful for investigating that crash.
cat.error-reports.name: Windows error reports
cat.error-reports.desc: Problem reports Windows collected about apps that stopped working. Already sent or no longer needed.
cat.gpu-shader-cache.name: Graphics shader cache
cat.gpu-shader-cache.desc: Shaders Windows and your graphics driver (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) prepared for games and apps. Prepared again the next time they run, so that first start may be a little slower. Only items untouched for a day are listed.
cat.edge-cache.name: Microsoft Edge cache
cat.edge-cache.desc: Pages and images Edge keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.chrome-cache.name: Google Chrome cache
cat.chrome-cache.desc: Pages and images Chrome keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.firefox-cache.name: Mozilla Firefox cache
cat.firefox-cache.desc: Pages and images Firefox keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.brave-cache.name: Brave cache
cat.brave-cache.desc: Pages and images Brave keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.vivaldi-cache.name: Vivaldi cache
cat.vivaldi-cache.desc: Pages and images Vivaldi keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.opera-cache.name: Opera cache
cat.opera-cache.desc: Pages and images Opera keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.yandex-cache.name: Yandex Browser cache
cat.yandex-cache.desc: Pages and images Yandex Browser keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.360-cache.name: 360 Browser cache
cat.360-cache.desc: Pages and images 360 Browser keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.qqbrowser-cache.name: QQ Browser cache
cat.qqbrowser-cache.desc: Pages and images QQ Browser keeps to open sites faster. Rebuilt as you browse; your history, passwords and sign-ins are kept.
cat.wechat-cache.name: WeChat cache
cat.wechat-cache.desc: Temporary files, and pages and images WeChat's built-in browser and mini programs keep. WeChat downloads them again when needed. Chat history is never touched.
cat.wechat-logs.name: WeChat logs
cat.wechat-logs.desc: Log files WeChat writes for troubleshooting.
cat.wechat-media.name: WeChat pictures and videos over 6 months old
cat.wechat-media.desc: Chat pictures and videos, by chat and month (chats show as codes). Chat history stays, but these pictures and videos will no longer open on this PC.
cat.wechat-files.name: Files received in WeChat over 6 months ago
cat.wechat-files.desc: Files received in chats, one by one. Chats still list them, but they must be downloaded again to open, and older ones may no longer be available.
cat.wecom-cache.name: WeCom cache
cat.wecom-cache.desc: Temporary files, and pages and images WeCom's built-in browser and mini programs keep. WeCom downloads them again when needed. Chat history, documents and synced files are never touched.
cat.wecom-logs.name: WeCom logs
cat.wecom-logs.desc: Log files WeCom writes for troubleshooting.
cat.wecom-media.name: WeCom pictures and videos over 6 months old
cat.wecom-media.desc: Chat pictures and videos, by month. Chat history stays, but these pictures and videos may no longer open on this PC.
cat.wecom-files.name: Files received in WeCom over 6 months ago
cat.wecom-files.desc: Files received in chats, one by one. Chats still list them, but they must be downloaded again to open, and older ones may no longer be available.
cat.qq-cache.name: QQ cache
cat.qq-cache.desc: Pages and images QQ's built-in browser keeps. Rebuilt as needed; chat history and received files are never touched.
cat.dingtalk-cache.name: DingTalk cache
cat.dingtalk-cache.desc: Pages and images DingTalk's built-in browser keeps. Rebuilt as needed; chat history and received files are never touched.
cat.feishu-cache.name: Feishu / Lark cache
cat.feishu-cache.desc: Pages and images Feishu / Lark's built-in browser keeps. Rebuilt as needed; chat history and received files are never touched.
cat.npm-cache.name: npm cache
cat.npm-cache.desc: Packages npm downloaded before. Downloaded again when a project needs them.
cat.pip-cache.name: pip cache
cat.pip-cache.desc: Python packages pip downloaded before. Downloaded again when needed.
cat.nuget-cache.name: NuGet HTTP cache
cat.nuget-cache.desc: Package lists and downloads NuGet cached. Your projects' installed packages are not touched.
cat.yarn-cache.name: Yarn cache
cat.yarn-cache.desc: Packages Yarn downloaded before. Downloaded again when a project needs them.
cat.gradle-cache.name: Gradle caches
cat.gradle-cache.desc: Dependencies and build caches Gradle downloaded (Android Studio). Downloaded again on the next build.
cat.vscode-cache.name: VS Code caches and logs
cat.vscode-cache.desc: Caches, old logs and crash reports of VS Code, VSCodium and Cursor, and extension downloads they keep. Rebuilt as needed; your settings, extensions and workspaces are not touched.
cat.go-cache.name: Go build cache
cat.go-cache.desc: Compiled packages Go keeps to build faster. Rebuilt on the next build.
cat.cargo-cache.name: Cargo registry cache
cat.cargo-cache.desc: Crates Cargo (Rust) downloaded before, and their unpacked sources. Downloaded again when a project needs them.
cat.steam-cache.name: Steam cache
cat.steam-cache.desc: Pages and images Steam keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; your games, saves and sign-in are kept.
cat.discord-cache.name: Discord cache
cat.discord-cache.desc: Pages and images Discord keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; your sign-in and settings are kept.
cat.slack-cache.name: Slack cache
cat.slack-cache.desc: Pages and images Slack keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; your sign-in and settings are kept.
cat.spotify-cache.name: Spotify cache
cat.spotify-cache.desc: Pages and images Spotify keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; downloaded music, sign-in and settings are kept.
cat.teams-cache.name: Microsoft Teams cache
cat.teams-cache.desc: Pages and images Microsoft Teams keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; your sign-in and settings are kept.
cat.cloudmusic-cache.name: NetEase Cloud Music cache
cat.cloudmusic-cache.desc: Pages and images NetEase Cloud Music keeps to load faster. Rebuilt as needed; downloaded music, sign-in and settings are kept.
cat.download-installers.name: Installers in Downloads
cat.download-installers.desc: Setup files (.exe, .msi, .msix) you downloaded. Not selected by default — keep the ones you still need.
cat.folder-node-modules.name: node_modules folders
cat.folder-node-modules.desc: Packages a Node.js project installed (next to its package.json). Not selected by default: installing them again needs the network, and an old project may no longer install the same.
cat.folder-dotnet-build.name: .NET build output (bin, obj)
cat.folder-dotnet-build.desc: Folders a .NET project builds into (next to its project file). Created again on the next build. Not selected by default: some older projects keep files they need right in bin.
cat.folder-target.name: Rust and Maven build output (target)
cat.folder-target.desc: Folders Cargo or Maven builds into (next to Cargo.toml or pom.xml). Created again on the next build.
cat.folder-gradle-build.name: Gradle build output (build, .gradle)
cat.folder-gradle-build.desc: Folders Gradle builds into (next to build.gradle). Created again on the next build.
cat.folder-python-cache.name: Python caches
cat.folder-python-cache.desc: __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache and .ruff_cache folders. Python and these tools create them again when needed.
cat.folder-office-temp.name: Office temporary files (~$)
cat.folder-office-temp.desc: Small hidden files Word, Excel and PowerPoint leave next to a document. Only ones untouched for a day are listed, so documents open now are not affected.
cat.folder-temp-files.name: Temporary files and thumbnail caches
cat.folder-temp-files.desc: .tmp files, Thumbs.db and .DS_Store. Only ones untouched for a day are listed.
settings.title: Settings
settings.startWithWindows.desc: Starts quietly in the notification area when you sign in. Nothing is scanned or cleaned until you ask.
settings.closeToTray: Keep running when the window is closed
settings.closeToTray.desc: The icon stays in the notification area. Right-click it and choose Exit to quit.
settings.reminder.desc: While SweeplyForWindows runs in the notification area, it looks now and then and shows a notification when at least 1 GB can be cleaned. Looking never moves anything.
reminder.title: Time to clean up
reminder.body: {0} can be cleaned. Click to see what.
settings.autoClean.desc: While SweeplyForWindows runs in the notification area, once a day it moves what is ticked by default to the Recycle Bin, except package caches and graphics shader caches (cleaned daily, they would only be downloaded or built again). Open apps and anything on the “Never clean” list are skipped. No list is shown first: a notification says what was moved, and it can be undone like any other clean.
autoClean.title: Cleaned up automatically
autoClean.body: {0} ({1} items) moved to the Recycle Bin. Click to see it; it can be undone in Settings.
settings.folderMenu: Add to the folder right-click menu
settings.folderMenu.desc: Right-click a folder, or empty space inside one, and choose “Clean up with SweeplyForWindows” to find leftovers such as node_modules, build output, Python caches and Office temporary files. On Windows 11 it's under “Show more options”.
tray.hint.title: SweeplyForWindows is still running
tray.hint.body: It's in the notification area. Right-click the icon to exit, or change this in Settings.
settings.trayDisplay.desc: Shows one live number instead of the app icon.
settings.trayToolTip: Show details when pointing at the icon
settings.trayToolTip.desc: Download and upload speed, CPU usage and disk writes, and drive and graphics card temperatures where Windows provides them.
settings.monitorBar.desc: A small bar that stays on top of other windows. Drag it anywhere; right-click it to hide it.
monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.subtitle: What this PC is doing right now. The charts show the last 2 minutes and are not saved.
monitor.gpu.note: The busiest engine, as in Task Manager
monitor.gpu.none: Windows doesn't report graphics card use on this PC
hw.temps.note: The processor's temperature can only be read with a kernel driver, which SweeplyForWindows doesn't install, so it isn't shown.
hw.health.note: From the drives' own health log (NVMe), read every minute while this tab is open. Life used is the maker's estimate of how much of the rated life is used up; it can pass 100%.
hw.health.none: No drive here keeps a health log that can be read (only internal NVMe drives do).
net.hint: Click an address to copy it.
net.others: Virtual adapters ({0}): virtual machines, VPNs, Bluetooth and the like
net.note: Read every 10 seconds while this tab is open, and right away when the network changes. Only what Windows already knows: nothing is sent.
net.ssidHidden: (Windows keeps it back: allow location access)
tools.ping.title: Ping
tools.ping.desc: Sends an echo to an address once a second: is it reachable, and how fast does it answer?
tools.fakeAddress: {0} is in 198.18.0.0/15, where proxies in TUN mode put the addresses they make up: the times show the proxy, not the network.
tools.note: Stops by itself when you leave the Monitor page or close the window. Packets go only to the address you enter.
tools.trace.title: Trace route
tools.trace.desc: Every router on the way to an address, and how fast each one answers (up to 30).
tools.trace.intercepted: It answered at the first hop although it isn't on your local network: a proxy in TUN mode or a VPN on this PC is probably answering for it, so the real route can't be seen.
tools.scan.title: Network scan
tools.scan.desc: Finds the devices on one adapter's network: one ping to each address, and Windows' own address lookup (ARP), so devices that ignore pings are found too. No ports are tried.
tools.scan.trimmed: This network is bigger: only the 254 addresses around this PC are scanned.
tools.scan.nothing: There is nothing to scan on this adapter.
tools.scan.none: No adapter with an IPv4 address is connected.
conn.filterHint: Filter by program, address, port or state
conn.showAll: Also listening ports, UDP and closed connections
conn.lookUpNames: Look up host names (asks the DNS server)
conn.note: Read every 2 seconds while this tab is open. A new connection is green for a moment; one that just closed, red. Click a program to see only its connections.
conn.reveal: Show the program in File Explorer
cap.title: Capture
cap.subtitle: See what goes over the network, packet by packet, the way Wireshark shows it.
cap.empty.title: No packets yet
cap.empty.body: Click Start capturing to see what this PC sends and receives (Windows may ask for administrator rights first). Or open a capture file (.pcapng, .pcap — what Wireshark and tcpdump save), or drop one on this page.
cap.truncated: Only the first {0} packets were read: the file is cut short, or bigger than what one capture keeps (200,000 packets, 256 MB).
cap.englishNote: Protocol names and fields are as in Wireshark.
cap.waitingAdmin: Waiting for you to allow it in Windows' prompt…
cap.waitingFirst: Capturing — waiting for the first packet.
cap.droppedNote: {0} packets were dropped: they came faster than they could be taken in.
cap.limit: Stopped at the limit ({0} packets or {1}). Save it, then start again.
cap.stopFirst: Stop capturing before opening a file.
cap.discard.text: The {0} packets captured last time aren't saved. Starting again clears them.
cap.error.Cancelled: Not started: capturing needs administrator rights, and Windows' prompt was cancelled.
cap.error.NeedAdmin: Windows refused: capturing needs administrator rights.
cap.error.NoAdapter: That adapter isn't connected now, or has no address. Pick another one.
cap.error.NoAddress: That adapter isn't connected now, or has no address. Pick another one.
cap.error.SocketFailed: Windows wouldn't capture on that adapter: {0}
cap.error.EtwFailed: Windows' built-in packet capture couldn't start: {0}
cap.error.FileFailed: The file to play back can't be read: {0}
cap.error.HelperLost: The capture helper stopped unexpectedly. What was captured is still here and can be saved.
cap.note.uncovered: Windows' built-in capture doesn't reach {0}, so raw sockets capture there: IPv4 packets only.
beh.title: Behavior
beh.subtitle: Record what a program does while it runs: which processes it starts, which files and registry entries it changes, which addresses it talks to. It only records; nothing is blocked or changed.
beh.target.launch: Start a program and record it
beh.full: Files and registry too (needs administrator rights; Windows asks first)
beh.autostop: Stop when the programs have all ended
beh.empty: Choose a program, click Start recording, then use it as usual. What it and the processes it starts do is listed here.
beh.notable.title: Worth a look
beh.notable.none: No autostart entries, services, scheduled tasks or the like were added.
beh.notable.hint: These are changes worth a look, not signs of harm: installers do them all the time.
beh.notable.Autostart.why: A registry entry that runs a program at every sign-in.
beh.notable.StartupFolder.why: Put in a Startup folder: opened at every sign-in.
beh.notable.Service.why: A Windows service created or changed; services can run from startup.
beh.notable.ScheduledTask.why: A scheduled task created or changed; it can run on a schedule or at startup.
beh.notable.Debugger.why: Image File Execution Options: running that program will start the one set here instead.
beh.notable.Hosts.why: The hosts file changed: names may now lead to other addresses.
beh.notable.Executable.why: A file that can be run (.exe, .dll, a script…) was written.
beh.notable.SystemFolder.why: Something in the Windows or Program Files folder changed.
beh.col.name: Name
beh.note.simple: Simple recording: the processes it starts, its connections, the names it looks up and how much it reads and writes. For files and the registry, tick the option above (needs administrator rights).
beh.note.simpleNoNames: Simple recording: the processes it starts, its connections and how much it reads and writes. For files, the registry and the names looked up, tick the option above (needs administrator rights).
beh.note.ended: The program and the processes it started have all ended; recording stopped.
beh.note.limit: Recorded for {0}, {1} events: the limit. Recording stopped.
beh.note.dropped: {0} events came too fast to be taken in.
beh.error.gone: That program has ended. Refresh the list and choose another.
beh.error.HelperLost: The recording helper stopped unexpectedly. What was recorded is still here.
beh.error.NeedAdmin: Windows refused: recording files and the registry needs administrator rights.
beh.error.Cancelled: Not started: recording files and the registry needs administrator rights, and Windows' prompt was cancelled. Untick that option for a simple recording.
beh.more: Only the first {0} are shown; export a CSV for all of them.
beh.usage: Read {0} · written {1} · CPU {2} s · peak memory {3}
beh.folders.title: Folders with the most changes
cap.filter.placeholder: Display filter, written as in Wireshark: dns, tcp.port == 443, process.name == "chrome.exe"
cap.filter.help: Enter applies it, Esc clears it. Protocols (dns, tls), fields (ip.addr, tcp.port, http.host), == != > < >= <=, contains, matches, in {…}, and / or / not and parentheses. process.name is the program.
cap.filter.unknownField: No packet passes. No packet here has {0} at all — is it spelt right?
cap.filter.error.UnexpectedEnd: It stops short: something is missing at the end.
cap.filter.error.BadValue: Character {0}: {1} is not a value to compare with (a number, an address, bytes or "text").
cap.filter.error.Unclosed: The {1} at character {0} is never closed.
cap.follow.title: {0} stream: {1} ⇄ {2}
cap.follow.summary: A sent {0}, B sent {1}, in {2} packets
cap.follow.encrypted: This connection is encrypted (TLS), so its content can't be read — as it should be. What shows is how much each end sent, and when.
cap.follow.more: … only the first {0} lines are shown; Save keeps everything …
cap.follow.hint: A is the end that sent first (for TCP, the one that opened the connection). Data sent again counts once; data that came early is put in its place.
cap.follow.none: This packet isn't part of a TCP or UDP stream.
cap.stats.noPrograms: This capture has no programs: only packets this app captures live have them.
cap.stats.col.name: Name
cap.problem.Retransmission.why: Data was sent again because it wasn't acknowledged in time: lost on the way, or a slow or busy network.
cap.problem.FastRetransmission.why: The other end kept saying something was missing, so it was sent again at once: a packet was lost.
cap.problem.OutOfOrder.why: Packets arrived in a different order than they were sent. Now and then it is harmless; often, it slows things down.
cap.problem.LostSegment.why: Data before this packet never showed up in the capture: lost on the network, or sent before capturing started.
cap.problem.AckedUnseen.why: The other end confirmed data the capture never saw: packets were missed while capturing, not on the network.
cap.problem.DuplicateAck.why: The receiver keeps asking for the same data: something before it is missing.
cap.problem.ZeroWindow.why: The receiving program can't keep up and asked the sender to pause (zero window).
cap.problem.Reset.why: A connection was cut off at once (RST): refused, or ended abruptly by one end or something in between.
cap.problem.IcmpError.why: The network sent word back that something couldn't be delivered: an address or port unreachable, or a packet that expired on the way.
cap.problem.DnsError.why: A DNS answer said no: no such name, or the server failed or refused. A few are normal (programs try names that don't exist).
monitor.temp.none: No temperatures can be read on this PC
support.title: Support SweeplyForWindows
support.body1: SweeplyForWindows is free and always will be — no ads, no accounts, no data collection.
support.body2: If it saved you some space or some time, you can buy the developer a coffee: WeChat Pay or Alipay in China, PayPal anywhere. Every coffee keeps the project going. Thank you!
support.other: Not in a position to donate? A star on GitHub, a bug report or a translation fix helps just as much.
about.title: About
about.tagline: A small, honest junk cleaner for Windows.
about.privacy: Never goes online by itself: no analytics, no accounts. Ping, trace route and the network scan send packets only when you start them, only to the addresses you choose.
about.license: Open source under the MIT license.
about.issues: Report a problem or suggest an idea
about.translation: Translations other than English and Chinese would love a review from native speakers.
